title: STRIDE: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Driving Edge Cases
abstract: arXiv:2610.22795v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In autonomous driving, perceiving surrounding objects is not enough: failing to understand how they move and interact over time can lead to dangerous decisions. Evaluating vision-language models (VLMs) therefore requires testing whether they connect past spatial observations to future consequences. Yet existing benchmarks often assess edge cases through basic perception questions or test temporal understanding in simple scenarios, leaving complex spatiotemporal reasoning underexplored. We introduce STRIDE (SpatioTemporal Reasoning In Driving Edge Cases), an object-centric benchmark for long-tail, safety-critical driving scenarios. STRIDE covers six task families: spatial perception, spatial understanding, temporal memory, temporal extrapolation, trajectory prediction, and scene-context awareness. tldr: STRIDE是一个面向自动驾驶安全关键长尾场景的以物体为中心的基准，通过空间感知、空间理解、时间记忆、时间外推、轨迹预测和场景上下文感知六大任务族，全面评估视觉语言模型连接过去空间观察与未来后果的复杂时空推理能力。
en_tdlr: STRIDE is an object-centric benchmark for long-tail, safety-critical driving scenarios that comprehensively evaluates vision-language models' complex spatiotemporal reasoning—connecting past spatial observations to future consequences—across six task families including spatial perception, temporal memory, extrapolation, and trajectory prediction.
